title: Ragas
evidence_excerpt: Ragas is a library that helps you move from "vibe checks" to systematic evaluation loops for your AI applications. Traditional evaluation metrics do not capture what matters for LLM applications. Manual evaluation does not scale. Ragas combines LLM-driven metrics with systematic experimentation to create a continuous improvement loop. Its RAG metric documentation includes Context Precision, Context Recall, Response Relevancy, and Faithfulness.

title: AI Risk Management Framework | NIST
evidence_excerpt: The NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) is intended for voluntary use and to improve the ability to incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use, and evaluation of AI products, services, and systems. Released on January 26, 2023, the Framework was developed through a consensus-driven, open, transparent, and collaborative process.

title: Security Checklist | Kubernetes
evidence_excerpt: Baseline checklist for ensuring security in Kubernetes clusters. The order of topics does not reflect an order of priority. Checklists are not sufficient for attaining a good security posture on their own. Since Kubernetes security is not "one size fits all", each category of checklist items should be evaluated on its merits. The checklist includes Authentication & Authorization, Pod security, Logs and auditing, and Images. It states that pod placement is done according to the tiers of sensitivity of the application, and that sensitive applications run isolated on nodes or with specific sandboxed runtimes. It also recommends regular container-image scanning and using pipeline compliance rules so only properly patched images reach production.
locator: Baseline checklist; Authentication & Authorization, Pod security, Logs and auditing, Pod placement, and Images sections; page metadata dateModified.

title: SP 800-190, Application Container Security Guide | CSRC
evidence_excerpt: Application Container Security Guide. Date Published: September 2017. This publication explains the potential security concerns associated with the use of containers and provides recommendations for addressing these concerns. Its listed control families include Access Control, Audit and Accountability, Identification and Authentication, Risk Assessment, System and Communications Protection, and System and Information Integrity.

title: LangGraph overview - Docs by LangChain
evidence_excerpt: The legacy LangGraph documentation page states: "Documentation has moved to docs.langchain.com." The current official overview describes LangGraph as a low-level orchestration framework and runtime for building, managing, and deploying long-running, stateful agents. It gives fine-grained control to mix deterministic, hand-coded steps with LLM-driven agentic steps in the same graph, and identifies durable execution, streaming, human-in-the-loop, and persistence as orchestration capabilities.

title: AutoGen - AutoGen
evidence_excerpt: AutoGen is a framework for building AI agents and applications. AgentChat is a programming framework for building conversational single and multi-agent applications. Core is an event-driven programming framework for building scalable multi-agent AI systems. The documented Core scenarios include deterministic and dynamic agentic workflows for business processes, research on multi-agent collaboration, and distributed agents for multi-language applications.
